sections.content:
27,615 people

were counted on the census as "driving instructors" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Driving instructors co-ordinate and undertake the instruction of people learning to drive cars, motorcycles, buses, fork-lifts and haulage vehicles.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "driving instructors" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "driving instructors", 19% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "driving instructors" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "driving instructors" included:

  • houseparents and residential wardens
  • directors in consultancy services
  • bus and coach drivers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "driving instructors" there were more men than women (77.3% compared with 22.7%).

This means "driving instructors" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "transport and mobile machine drivers and operatives".

Men made up 77.3% and women made up 22.7% of "driving instructors"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "driving instructors" included:

  • farm workers
  • senior officers in fire, ambulance, prison and related services
  • warehouse operatives

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "driving instructors", 11.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (60.5% compared with 39.5%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (84.2%) than an employee (15.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
